record.paper_title: Statements and open problems on decidable sets X ⊆ N that contain informal notions and refer to the current knowledge on X
record.original_question: Are there infinitely many prime Fermat numbers, that is, infinitely many primes of the form 2^(2^k) + 1 with k ∈ N?

evidence.quote: It is open whether or not there are infinitely many primes of the form 2^(2^k) + 1, see [7, p. 158] and [11, p. 74].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a nonnegative integer $k$, the $k$-th Fermat number is defined by $F_k = 2^{2^k} + 1$. A Fermat prime is a Fermat number that is prime. The known Fermat primes are $F_0 = 3$, $F_1 = 5$, $F_2 = 17$, $F_3 = 257$, and $F_4 = 65537$, and no further Fermat prime has been discovered.

Determine whether there exist infinitely many nonnegative integers $k$ such that $F_k = 2^{2^k} + 1$ is prime.
artifact.status_search_result: It is a classical and well-known open problem in number theory whether infinitely many Fermat primes exist; in fact, it is even unknown whether any Fermat prime beyond $F_4$ exists. Only the five Fermat primes $F_0,\dots,F_4$ are known, and $F_k$ has been shown to be composite for many subsequent $k$.

status_evidence.title: Fermat number - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: It is widely believed but unproven that F_0, ..., F_4 are the only Fermat primes; whether infinitely many Fermat primes exist is an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The infinitude (and even existence beyond F_4) of Fermat primes is an open problem.
